first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A company that plans weddings in Portugal for Aussies, Americans and Brits, with one advisor looking after us. Palaces in Sintra, cliffs in the Algarve. The first thing they tell me is the legal paperwork takes a month and lots of people just do a symbolic one there and sign at home, which is actually handy to know.

attention_map.quote: Many couples hold a symbolic ceremony in Portugal and marry legally at home.
attention_map.why: Straight away I know we don't have to deal with Portuguese paperwork if we don't want to. And 'one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend' is what I want: one person, not a dozen suppliers in another time zone.
I can tap '30 to 60' guests, fine, but it just takes me to a form. Nothing comes back to tell me whether 30 to 60 is doable or what it costs.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: It's the same sentence I just read in the hero. There's no number, no review, nothing that tells me they've actually done this.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal (Pena, Monserrate, Queluz, Douro, Algarve)
attention_map.quote: Romantic palaces in the Sintra hills that can be booked for a wedding
attention_map.why: Getting married in a palace is different. That is the not-a-standard-package feeling we want. Then 'roof works with scaffolding run to the first quarter of 2027' makes me think, ok, that one's off the list for now.

Five times in a row. That is the one line on each card I actually care about and it's blank. And 'Best months: spring and autumn, as a national guide' repeats on every card too, so the cards don't really help me tell the regions apart.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra. Nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: Honest, and I like knowing that before I fall in love with it. Still no idea how many people a palace holds or what it costs to book.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: Australian, US and UK passport holders can visit visa-free for up to 90 days
attention_map.why: Good, our guests won't need visas. The rest repeats what I already read about palaces and the Douro.

attention_map.section: Pick the Setting / venue contract checks
attention_map.quote: exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill
attention_map.why: This is exactly the kind of thing that blows a budget out, and it's good that someone checks it for us. But it scares me a bit, because there are still no numbers anywhere.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: When to go, Getting there, Entry rules
attention_map.quote: Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide
attention_map.why: Useful for guests. But there's nothing about how long it takes to get from Australia to Lisbon, or how far Faro or Porto venues are from the airport.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: Marrying legally
attention_map.quote: The Australian Embassy in Lisbon can issue a CNI, and DFAT also issues CNIs in Australia.
attention_map.why: The Australian bit is reassuring. But it's a wall of registry rules, US and UK paragraphs and gov links, and I'm reading it on my phone at 10pm. I'll leave the paperwork for the advisor.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: I opened the Costs tab for one thing and there isn't a single number in it. Not even a rough range. That's the moment I'd think, here we go, it's going to be expensive and they won't say.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package.
attention_map.why: I like the Friday dinner, Saturday wedding, Sunday brunch idea, it sounds like us. But no package plus no price means I can't even guess what the 'all in' would be.

attention_map.quote: Guest website in Wonderland Studio: share the schedule, travel and entry rules in one place. [Start for free]
attention_map.why: Where guests stay is half answered ('many quintas have rooms... nearby hotels for everyone else'). Then suddenly there's a sign-up for some other product. Not what I'm here for yet.
Not relevant to us, just scrolled past.

attention_map.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue.
attention_map.why: This is the bit that answers our time zones worry. The three steps are clear. But who is this person? No name, no face, no idea if they've ever been to Portugal.

attention_map.quote: Placeholder: Budget, dates you have in mind, anything else
attention_map.why: Short enough and no phone number required, which I appreciate. I'd fill it in if I already knew our budget fits. Right now I'd be asking blind.

attention_map.quote: There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count, the region, the season...
attention_map.why: The cost FAQ gives the same non-answer as the tab. The small wedding and Sintra palace ones are fine.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links on a page where I'm meant to trust these people with our wedding money. Feels like a magazine, not a planner.

questions_answered.question: What does this cost all in, and what is included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: No from price, no range, no inclusions. The Costs tab and FAQ 4 only list what cost 'depends on'. 'There is no set Portugal package.'

questions_answered.question: Can it fit our guest count?
questions_answered.evidence: Every region card says 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor'. No palace or venue capacity anywhere. Only that witnesses are optional and small weddings are welcome.

questions_answered.question: Who would actually plan this with us, and what do they do?
questions_answered.evidence: The role is clear: 'your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue', walks us through the legal route and 'check each venue contract for rooms, buy-outs, minimums and VAT'. But there's no name, no person and no track record.

questions_answered.question: How do our guests get there and where do they stay?
questions_answered.evidence: Four airports (LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC), visa-free for Australians, 'Many quintas have rooms... with nearby hotels for everyone else', Lisbon venues '15 to 30 minutes from the city centre'. Nothing on getting there from Australia or on transfer times outside Lisbon.

questions_answered.question: Is our budget realistic for this place?
questions_answered.evidence: No figures at all on the launch page, so I can't tell if 50k for 60 people is a laugh or plenty.

objections_triggered.objection: I don't know if my budget is possible for this many people

trust_signals_noticed: Who my planner is and the steps: the three-step 'How It Works' and the advisor's role (no name though)
Travel from a major airport: airport codes per region and 'Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide'
Named spaces: 'upper gardens and Throne Room' at Queluz, but without capacities
Honest caveats: Monserrate scaffolding to early 2027, state events can cancel palace bookings
Australian-specific legal info with Smartraveller and Australian Embassy links, 'Checked October 2026'
turn_offs_noticed: No price signal at all: not a from price, not a range, not even third-party figures at launch
No guest numbers for any region or venue
Long on a phone: the Marrying legally tab is mostly US and UK detail I scroll through
Celebrity trending links (Ronaldo, Perrie Edwards) at the bottom
A 'Start for free' sign-up for Wonderland Studio in the middle of the guest section

emotional_response.felt: Excited by the Sintra palaces and the three-day weekend idea, then flat once I got to the Costs tab and found nothing. Relieved about the one advisor and the symbolic ceremony option.
emotional_response.stress_free: Partly. The advisor checking contracts and handling the legal route sounds stress-free. Not knowing the cost is the opposite.
emotional_response.authentically_us: The Friday dinner, Saturday wedding, Sunday brunch shape feels like us.

payload.decision_reason: It's pretty and the advisor setup is what we want, so I'd screenshot the Sintra bits and send it to my partner. But there is no price anywhere and every region says 'Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor', so I can't tell if Portugal fits 60 people on our budget. I'm not filling in a form just to find out if we can afford it. If the Italy or Greece pages give me a number first, Portugal probably drops off the list.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Ok this is gorgeous, a palace in Sintra, who knew. One person handling everything, yes please. But how much?? I tapped Costs and it just says it 'depends on five things'. Of course it depends, I just want a ballpark. And how many people fit? Every card says ask your advisor. Saving it to send to him, but I'm not enquiring blind.
